description: Given a list of directory info strings, each containing a directory path followed by files with their content in parentheses, find all groups of duplicate files (files with the same content). Return a list of groups, where each group contains file paths with the same content.
intuition: Group files by their content using a hash map. Parse each path string to extract the directory, filename, and content, then map content to the list of full file paths. Any content with more than one file path indicates duplicates.
approach: Parse each path string to extract directory, filename, and content. Use a hash map from content to list of file paths. Return only groups with more than one file.
jsWalkthrough:
Example: paths = ["root/a 1.txt(abcd) 2.txt(efgh)","root/c 3.txt(abcd)"]

Process "root/a 1.txt(abcd) 2.txt(efgh)":
  directory = "root/a"
  token "1.txt(abcd)": name="1.txt", content="abcd", path="root/a/1.txt"
  token "2.txt(efgh)": name="2.txt", content="efgh", path="root/a/2.txt"

Process "root/c 3.txt(abcd)":
  directory = "root/c"
  token "3.txt(abcd)": name="3.txt", content="abcd", path="root/c/3.txt"

contentToFilePaths:
  "abcd" → ["root/a/1.txt","root/c/3.txt"] (length 2 → duplicate!)
  "efgh" → ["root/a/2.txt"] (length 1 → not duplicate)
Return [["root/a/1.txt","root/c/3.txt"]]
explanation:
1. Parse each path string: first token is directory, rest are "filename(content)".
2. Split filename and content, and map content to full file paths.
3. After processing all paths, return groups with 2+ files (duplicates).
4. Files with the same content are grouped together.
timeComplexity: O(n * k) where n is paths and k is average files per path
hints: Parse the directory path and file content from each string.
Use a hash map to group files by content.
Return only groups with more than one file.
